question: When solving an AC circuit containing a Resistor ($R$) and an Inductor ($L$) in series, why is it incorrect to simply add the peak voltage across the resistor ($V_R$) and the peak voltage across the inductor ($V_L$) algebraically ($V_{total} = V_R + V_L$) to find the source voltage?

options.A: Because the voltages are vectors pointing in the same direction.
options.B: Because the peak voltages occur at different instants of time due to a phase difference.
options.C: Because the inductor consumes zero power while the resistor consumes power.
options.D: Because the frequency of voltage across the inductor is different from that across the resistor.
